transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~54m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (CSM), Luca (SE); Marta (Valerian Head of Platform), Omar (SRE), Sophie (CISO)
Links shared: onboarding-runbook-v1.pdf (drive), security-pack-redwood.zip (link), sample-bench-script.py (link)

Summary: quick activation kickoff focused on private/VPC deployment constraints, latency SLOs, and an upcoming benchmark run. Customer emphasized strict key management + audit retention needs. Team aligned on pilot scope and next-step dates.

00:00 Jordan: okay everyone thanks for joining, uh let's do quick intros then roll into the plan, we have about 50 minutes so should be fine
00:12 Marta: thanks, yes i'll kick off i'm marta, head of platform at Valerian, we own infra for the security product, excited to get this moving
00:20 Omar: omar, sres, i'll run the bench and the network bits, glad to be here
00:24 Sophie: sophie, ciso, jumping in for security constraints and compliance questions
00:30 Jordan: great, i'm jordan on the AE side, priya our csm will handle onboarding cadence, and luca our se will own the benchmark and private deploy details
00:40 Priya: hi all, will follow up with onboarding timeline and contact matrix
00:46 Luca: hey team, quick note - i'll probably ask for a short runbook of expected load shapes, e.g., chat-style bursts vs steady embedding workloads

02:05 Jordan: high level agenda: confirm pilot scope, network & security requirements, benchmark plan, and next steps. Marta, can you re-state the primary success criteria?
02:18 Marta: yes, main things are: p95 sub-200ms on our auth proxy for the customer-facing chat, end-to-end token cost not to exceed our target (we have a tight budget), and full audit logs for all inference requests retained for 13 months per compliance
02:35 Sophie: also need KMS/HSM integration for key material, and option for on-prem key keeper; we can't have keys in a third-party control plane without HSM-backed separation
02:50 Jordan: understood, those are pretty standard for private deployments. Luca, quick comment on the p95 target — sub-200ms is challenging depending on model and sequence length, right?
03:05 Luca: yeah, so depends a lot on model choice, quantization, batch behavior, and whether you'll accept a trimmed context. If you're doing 1-2 prompt exchanges at short sequences, we can get close on dedicated GPU pools, but on small instances or with high concurrency it could stretch past 200ms
03:28 Omar: just to flag, our front-end does prefix caching so we expect a lot of repeated prefixes, which might help. We also have spikes at 9am and 5pm roughly
03:40 Priya: that caching is great news — Redwood support automatic prefix/KV cache so that reduces per-token cost and latency if configured properly

05:02 Marta: about hosting — we want the private deployment in our AWS VPC, minimum exposure. Is Redwood private full control plane in our network or is there still a managed plane?
05:15 Jordan: good question. Redwood Private gives an option for customer-managed control plane. For your case, you can choose a private control plane deployed in your VPC with no control-plane traffic leaving the VPC, or a hybrid where control is in Redwood cloud but data plane stays in your region.
05:36 Sophie: must clarify — hybrid is not acceptable unless we have contractual guarantees re: key handling and audit access
05:44 Jordan: noted, we'll put hybrid as a fall-back only. We'll include KMS/HSM integration details in the security pack.

07:10 Luca: for the benchmark plan i'll propose two runs: a latency-focused run (single-tenant, p95 measurement, cold-starts) and a throughput run (sustained concurrency to observe batching behavior). We'll instrument token-level latency and cost-per-token.
07:28 Omar: good. Can we run a synthetic chat workload and a real replay of sanitized logs? we can provide 24 hours of traffic sample
07:35 Luca: yes replay is ideal to replicate real KV cache hits and request shapes
07:40 Jordan: timeline — propose bench week of 9/22. Luca, you'll own coordination with Omar?
07:46 Luca: yes i'll coordinate. I'll also send the sample-bench-script.py and instructions to set up a small canary deployment

09:00 Sophie: thoughts on audit log retention and format? we need immutable logs with hashing and access control, and retention to 13 months
09:12 Priya: Redwood supports audit logs in both S3 and push-based syslog; retention configurable. For immutable logs, we can integrate with your existing object lock or put a write-once policy. We'll include details in the security pack
09:28 Marta: also need RBAC mapped to our identity provider - sso/saml mapping
09:34 Jordan: yes we integrate with SAML/SCIM for RBAC. Priya will share the mapping guide.

11:00 Omar: network specifics: we want VPC endpoints only, no public internet egress. Also need TLS mutual auth for the data plane
11:12 Luca: mutual TLS is supported, and we can use your CA or generate certs within the cluster, depending on your policies. We'll want to test MTLS and ephemeral cert rotation during bench
11:28 Marta: any constraints about port ranges or egress rules? our security team wants minimal allowed rules
11:34 Luca: typically just outbound to the model nodes on the overlay and internal control plane ports; i'll send a minimal firewall allowlist

13:10 Jordan: budget question — Marta mentioned tight token cost target. we offer both hosted per-token and dedicated reserved capacity. For heavy steady workloads, dedicated capacity tends to be cheaper per-token, with predictable throughput
13:28 Marta: do you have ballpark numbers? we need to present to finance
13:33 Jordan: i'll share the dedicated capacity pricing sheet after the call. For pilot we often do a short dedicated reserve, or run on dedicated burst enabled mode. I'll include examples with quantization profiles that lower cost
13:44 Omar: quantization — do you support 4-bit or q4-ish profiles, and does that affect latency much?
13:52 Luca: we support several quantization profiles. 4-bit (q4) can dramatically reduce memory and cost; latency impact depends on runtime kernels and sequence length — sometimes slight speed-ups, sometimes tradeoffs for attention kernels. We'll recommend specific profiles after we see sample model/sequence lengths

15:05 Marta: question on rollouts — we want canary traffic splitting and automatic fallback to smaller models if latencies spike. Is that supported?
15:18 Jordan: yes, Redwood Console supports traffic routing policies, canary deploys, A/B, and automatic fallback to configured model variants or a lower-cost serving tier
15:30 Sophie: and how are model versions handled? auditably pinned?
15:35 Luca: you can pin exact model hashes and the deployment records are versioned with metadata. Console retains rollout history for audits. We'll include a screenshot in the runbook

17:00 Omar: about observability — token-level cost breakdown and tracing hooks. do we need to instrument anything special?
17:10 Priya: Console exposes token counts, per-route latency histograms, and tracing hooks. For distributed tracing, you can forward spans to your collector; we'll provide a sample instrumentation library
17:25 Marta: retention on metrics — we need 12 months of metrics for incident review
17:30 Priya: we have an advanced observability add-on that extends retention; i'll include options and pricing

19:12 Luca: small note — cold start behavior can add 100-400ms depending on GPU spin and KV warm-up. Our bench will simulate cold and warm starts
19:25 Omar: ok we'll look for that in the results

21:00 Sophie: security red flags — any external data residency concerns? all inference must be processed in our us-east-1 region, and no logs exported outside the region
21:12 Jordan: understood. We'll ensure region pinning and data plane resources provisioned in us-east-1 only

23:10 Marta: timeline to pilot: if bench goes well we want a 6-week pilot then potentially ramp to production. Is that realistic?
23:22 Jordan: yes typical pilot length is 4-8 weeks depending on integrations. We'll propose a 6-week pilot with checkpoints at week 2 and week 4

25:00 Luca: i'll draft the benchmark plan: inputs: replay data (you provide sample logs), workload parameters (concurrency, sequence distributions), outputs: p50/p95/p99 latencies, cost per 1K tokens, cold vs warm, KV hit ratios, memory/CPU consumption, and failure modes. Will include runbook to reproduce
25:20 Omar: i'll sanitize logs and provide them by 9/19
25:28 Luca: perfect

27:40 Jordan: any blockers from legal or procurement?
27:46 Marta: procurement is okay with us starting pilot under a short-term MSA, but Sophie will need data-processing addendum and security annex signed
27:58 Sophie: yes DPA with the right clauses around KMS, subprocessing, and audit access
28:06 Jordan: we'll route that to legal and attach the security pack. Priya will coordinate

30:10 Priya: action items recap: jordan runbook + pricing, luca bench plan + script, priya security pack, marta provide logs and network diagram. Dates included in the action item list
30:25 Marta: yes we'll aim for those dates

32:00 Omar: small technical Q: if we need HSM in our account, do you support bringing-your-own-HSM (BYOHSM) or do you require Redwood-managed keys?
32:12 Luca: we support both. BYO-HSM + KMS integration is supported; for hybrid there's an extra config step for key proxying. We'll document the steps and crypto expectations

34:40 Sophie: also need to ensure access controls for the runbook and who at Redwood can see entitlements, please minimize who has access to PII or sensitive logs during bench
34:52 Priya: we'll limit access to the SE and a named operations engineer; the runbook links will respect your SSO/entitlement mapping

36:00 Jordan: pricing note — if you go dedicated we'll reserve capacity for the pilot and you get predictable throughput; if the pilot is small we can do a temporary burst-enabled setup to avoid big upfronts
36:20 Marta: finance prefers predictable but pilot has to be light on budget. maybe a small reserved block plus pay-as-you-go overlay
36:32 Jordan: we can propose that in the pricing sheet

38:10 Luca: can we talk model variants for a sec — for production you could route to smaller fine-tuned variant for simple queries and bigger model for complex synthesis, automatic routing possible
38:25 Omar: that seems useful for cost control
38:30 Marta: yes we'd like routing by intent if possible
38:34 Luca: we support rule-based routing and ML-powered classifiers as a routing hook; for pilot we'll suggest a simple rule-based split

40:50 Sophie: compliance Q: do you have annual pen test reports and third-party attestations?
40:58 Priya: yes we have SOC2 and ISO certs; the security pack includes the summary and we can arrange an NDA to share the full attestations
41:12 Sophie: good, we'll need to review under an NDA

43:00 Jordan: ok nearing end — let's confirm dates: jordan to send runbook and pricing by 9/18, priya security pack by 9/19, marta provide sanitized logs and network diagram by 9/20, bench week scheduled for 9/22 with luca and omar
43:18 Marta: confirmed

44:00 Omar: quick note on orchestration: during bench we'll test autoscaling behavior, can you simulate burst + cooldown?
44:10 Luca: yes we'll configure autoscaler to mirror your expected bursts and measure cooldowns and cost impact

46:30 Priya: final recap — i'll create a shared channel and calendar invite for the bench and pilot planning, and i'll attach all docs. Any other questions?
46:40 Marta: none from me, thanks everyone
46:45 Sophie: none, thank you
46:48 Jordan: great, thanks all. we'll follow up with the docs and meet next Tuesday for the bench run.

End of transcript.
